title: Carbon Brake Wear Reading Inconsistent Between Turnarounds
abstract: Fault isolation for a brake wear reading that moves between turnarounds without corresponding use, separating a datum problem from a genuinely uneven stack.

sections.purpose: This procedure isolates the cause of a carbon brake wear reading that changes between turnarounds by more than the use in between can explain.
sections.fault_description: The wear reading taken at one turnaround does not agree with the reading taken at the previous one, and the difference is larger than the landings in between can account for. On aircraft at the delivered wear pin datum this is usually the datum itself: the pin reads against the pressure plate, which moves as the torque tube attachment relaxes, so the reading depends on how hard the brake was applied when it was taken and on how much the flange has relaxed since. On aircraft at the relocated datum the reading is independent of the attachment, and an inconsistent reading there means the stack really is wearing unevenly.
sections.isolation_procedure: 1. Confirm from the aircraft record which wear pin datum standard is fitted. 2. Confirm that both readings were taken with the correct acceptance table and with the specified brake pressure applied. 3. Where the delivered datum is fitted, take three fresh readings at the specified pressure and confirm they agree with each other. 4. Where the fresh readings disagree with each other, the pressure plate is moving: check the torque tube flange attachment for relaxation. 5. Where the fresh readings agree but disagree with the previous record, the flange has relaxed since: plan the wear pin datum relocation and treat the current reading as the valid one. 6. Where the relocated datum is fitted, measure the stack thickness at three positions spaced one hundred and twenty degrees apart. 7. Where the three positions differ by more than the figure in the limits table, the stack is wearing unevenly: examine the brake for a seized piston and check the regulator D3240112571209. 8. Check the pump 1GB and the inboard pump 584GB for leakage that would leave one piston dragging. 9. WARNING: DO NOT APPROACH A BRAKE USED WITHIN THE LAST HOUR. 10. Where nothing is found, remove the brake for shop examination and send the three readings with it. 11. CAUTION: DO NOT COMPARE A READING FROM ONE DATUM STANDARD WITH A READING FROM THE OTHER. THEY ARE NOT THE SAME MEASUREMENT.
sections.dispatch_note: The aircraft may be dispatched where the smallest of three fresh readings is above the acceptance limit for the standard fitted. Dispatch is not permitted on a single reading where the previous record disagrees, because the smaller of the two must be assumed until it is resolved.

type_data.fault_symptom: Brake wear reading inconsistent between consecutive turnarounds

possible_causes.cause: Wear pin reading against a moving pressure plate on the delivered datum
Uneven stack wear from a dragging piston
Reading taken without the specified brake pressure applied

dispatch.dispatch_condition: Smallest of three fresh readings above the acceptance limit for the datum standard fitted
